title: Rivers, film, and the walk from the market
description: Short questions on what flies, what floats, and what stays a product.

questions.question: Bags in a river tree. Why does film travel farther than a jerry can?
options: It is light — wind and water both move it
It is heavier than a can
It melts in the sun into water
Collectors fight over it first
questions.answer: It is light — wind and water both move it
questions.explanation: Film leaves a hand and keeps going. Contain it at the house.

questions.question: A river full of bottles. What would have stopped this load?
options: A dry PET pile at the door, before the drain
Waiting for the sea to sort them
Mixing them with oil cans
Crushing them into the mud
questions.answer: A dry PET pile at the door, before the drain
questions.explanation: The cheapest cleanup is the one that never enters the water.

questions.question: PET bottles in a mesh cage, several colours. Is the cage mixed grade?
options: No — colours of PET can share a grade
Yes — each colour is a new polymer
Yes — green means glass
No — mesh turns everything into HDPE
questions.answer: No — colours of PET can share a grade
questions.explanation: Colour is the second sort. The cage is still PET.

questions.question: A PP tub. Where does it not belong?
options: Inside a PET bottle sack
In a small PP pile of cups and tubs
Rinsed and dry, foil lid off
Residual, if there is no mark and you will not guess
questions.explanation: PP is not PET. A food pot is not a water bottle.

questions.question: An opaque milk-style bottle. After you rinse it, which pile?
options: HDPE, with the other kitchen jugs
PET, because it held a drink
Film, because it is not clear
Glass, because milk used to be glass
questions.answer: HDPE, with the other kitchen jugs
questions.explanation: Drink is not a grade. The wall and the triangle are.

questions.question: A recycling bin with a mark. What breaks the bin?
options: A mixed liner of bottles, bags, and a charger
A bag of one clean grade the bin is for
Rinsed items
A lid that matches the stream
questions.answer: A mixed liner of bottles, bags, and a charger
questions.explanation: The mark is a stream. A lucky-dip liner is the old bin with a new sticker.

questions.question: Pressed PET, close enough to see bottle necks. Why press?
options: Volume that can travel — air is not a product
Pressing changes the grade to HDPE
Pressing cleans food off
Pressing makes film
questions.answer: Volume that can travel — air is not a product
questions.explanation: A bale is air squeezed out of one grade.

questions.question: A facility heap at the door. What should have happened at the house?
options: The same pull-apart, while the plastic was still clean
Nothing — houses cannot sort
Burning, so the yard stays empty
Hiding film inside bottles
questions.answer: The same pull-apart, while the plastic was still clean
questions.explanation: Household sorting is the first station of the same factory.

questions.question: Nurdles in grit. Are they household bottles yet?
options: No — they spilled before a bottle existed
Yes — they are crushed PET
Yes — they are washed sand
No — they are seeds
questions.answer: No — they spilled before a bottle existed
questions.explanation: Factory-start plastic, not a kitchen sort. Still a leak the water will take.

questions.question: White and blue HDPE cans, already in separate bales. What skill is that?
options: Colour after grade — same polymer, cleaner pellet
Two different grades pretending to be one
A photo trick
Proof that colour does not matter
questions.answer: Colour after grade — same polymer, cleaner pellet
questions.explanation: The yard is showing the second sort. You can start it on a balcony.
